svg.text: Figure 2 · Plot → New: the probe set and the node picker
probe: line · closed: no · 49 rows · othId 0
othId 0 is present in the othd
snaps to the nearest row and shows the distance
probe: line · body cyl · s from the beam origin, along its axis
discovered from the file by series.scan(), not hard-coded
The dropdown lists othd.*.map in the case.
Its header gives the probe type, whether the
curve closes, the row count and the othId.
The othId is predicted from the .def, so it is
checked against the othd’s real groups.
line → along the axis helix → unrolled
cloud → same, with no joining line
Coordinates alone cannot tell these apart,
which is why the map declares the type.
the map is built on, so a probe set resolves
to its body: axis, origin, length, radius.
That turns a generic projection into arc
length along the beam. Without it the
picker still works, on x/y/z axes.
The othd stores records positionally, so the
reader indexes by row. The map carries the
solver node id and the undeformed x,y,z.
Both are shown so neither is mistaken for
Click a marker, or drag a box or lasso for a
span of rows. Typing a coordinate snaps to
the nearest row and reports the distance,
so a bad guess is visible rather than silent.
Undeformed coordinates: the map states them, and the othd displacement is added for the moved position.
